summary: David J. Kalupahana was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Ceylon and completed his PhD at the University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. He held posts at Ceylon and Hawaiʻi.

David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. Attested in 2007, he directed the Center for the Development of Asian Studies and taught within the University System of Georgia.

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He held academic posts at SOAS, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University (1969–2002), and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies in 1993.

David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, also studying under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman. He has held a post at Smith College.

David Kopf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1960 to 1964. He held an academic post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 2003.
David L. Gosling is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge, attested in 2001.

David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona (circa 1989–1993) and Indiana University Bloomington (circa 1993–2022).

David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, and has served as a professor of religious studies at Franklin & Marshall College.

David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Southampton and Cambridge. He was a professor at SOAS, University of London from 1950 to 1982 and founded the Institute of Tibetan Studies.

David Ludden is a historian and Indologist who studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and New York University beginning in 2007.

David M. DiValerio works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia, where he earned his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee.
David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, holding appointments as professor and chair of religious studies.
David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as Director of the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as President Emeritus of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

David Max Moerman is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Barnard College and Columbia University, serving as professor and department chair.

David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian who studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was a professor at El Colegio de México from 1970 to 2010.

David Ownby is a historian and sinologist who studied at Vanderbilt and earned his Ph.D. from Harvard. He held posts at Southern Methodist University and the Université de Montréal (1994–2023), later joining the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology.

David P. Chandler is a historian who studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Monash University (circa 1972–1997), the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Cornell University, and Johns Hopkins University.

David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg from 1992 to 2007.

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa as well as Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He has held posts at Naropa University and the Nitartha Institute.
